title: The forecast gain from a second decay term depended on exponent settings in Puerto Rico on days 7-30 at magnitude 3 or more
abstract: We tested whether a second decay term for the 11 January 2020 magnitude 5.9 event improved a simple forecast of Puerto Rico earthquakes. We fit one-term and two-term rate models on days 1-7 after the 7 January mainshock reference time. We tested days 7-30. The primary sample used magnitude 3 or more within 50 km of a fixed center. It had 211 training events and 317 test events. With a fitted common decay exponent, the second term raised the test log score by 54.43 nats. The conditional 95% three-day block interval was -2.70 to 108.18 nats. The one-term model predicted 590.75 events; the two-term model predicted 182.42. Both count estimates had large errors. With the exponent fixed at one, the second term reduced the score by 17.30 nats. Thus the gain was not stable across the tested exponent settings. This single-sequence test uses a revised catalog and simple Poisson rate models. It does not test a full ETAS forecast, identify a physical cause, or support an operational hazard forecast. The package gives exact source bytes, code, daily scores, block samples, a figure, and independent numerical checks.

display.caption: Observed and predicted daily counts on held-out days, and log score changes across all planned settings. Positive scores favor two decay terms. The intervals hold fitted models fixed. They do not include parameter or catalog error.
